title: Responsive Images and Media
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of Responsive Images and Media and recognize when it is useful.
Apply a relevant property, selector, or technique from this lesson in a small stylesheet.
Inspect the browser result and explain one behavior, limitation, or compatibility consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore Responsive Images and Media through a small CSS example, a visual guide, and one practical check. You do not need to memorize every property at once; focus on the decision the browser is making.
content.why_it_matters: Responsive Images and Media helps you build interfaces that remain understandable, maintainable, and usable as content and viewport conditions change.

content_blocks.title: Responsive layout decisions
content_blocks.alt_text: Let content determine layout changes; do not design only for named devices. Labels show the concept flow.
content_blocks.caption: Use the labeled steps as a reasoning guide; detailed behavior is described in the lesson.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Responsive design adapts to available space and user preferences, not to a list of device names. Start with content that fits, add breakpoints only when the layout needs them, and test zoom, orientation, and narrow widths.

content_blocks.title: A useful way to practice
content_blocks.text: Start with one element or component. Use the concepts in this lesson—flexible image widths, max-width: 100%, image aspect ratios—and change one declaration at a time. Compare the page before and after the change.

items.title: Flexible image widths
items.text: Calculate the rendered box, not only its declared width; check padding, border, min/max constraints, and the parent layout.

items.title: max-width: 100%
items.text: Calculate the rendered box, not only its declared width; check padding, border, min/max constraints, and the parent layout.

items.title: Image aspect ratios
items.text: Calculate the rendered box, not only its declared width; check padding, border, min/max constraints, and the parent layout.

items.title: Video and embedded-content sizing
items.text: Connect video and embedded-content sizing to the main idea in responsive images and media, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

items.title: Preventing media overflow
items.text: Connect preventing media overflow to the main idea in responsive images and media, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

content_blocks.code:
.media-frame { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0.75rem; }
.media-frame img, .media-frame video { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: center; }
content_blocks.expected_output: The frame keeps a consistent aspect ratio while the media fills it; use object-position when the important subject would otherwise be cropped.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Put this snippet in styles.css and link it from a minimal index.html file with a viewport meta tag. Add elements whose classes match the selectors, open the page in a modern browser, and inspect computed styles. This lesson editor displays the expected result as a guide; it is not a server-side arbitrary-code runner.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original CSS snippet, save the file, and repeat the test. Remove temporary debugging rules before keeping a final version.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Start with a fluid base layout and add a breakpoint only when the content needs a different arrangement.

content.task: Try it yourself: build a small example that demonstrates Responsive Images and Media. Use the simplest relevant selector and one or more declarations, inspect the browser result, and explain it in your own words.
task_acceptance_criteria: The stylesheet uses valid CSS syntax for the chosen feature.
The intended element or state visibly changes when the rule applies.
The behavior is checked with browser tools or a documented manual checklist.
hints: Write the smallest rule that can demonstrate the concept.
Inspect which element matched and which declaration won before adding more selectors.
For a developing or optional feature, check browser support and preserve a useful fallback.
content.expected_output: The frame keeps a consistent aspect ratio while the media fills it; use object-position when the important subject would otherwise be cropped.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to connect a visual change to its cause.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one property, save, and compare again.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the last rule always wins.
common_mistakes.why: The cascade also considers origin, importance, layers and selector specificity; scope and source order may also matter.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect matched declarations and computed styles before changing the stylesheet.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only one viewport or interaction state.
common_mistakes.why: A rule can work at one width and fail when content, focus, zoom or preferences change.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the check at narrow and wide widths and include keyboard focus or reduced-motion checks when relevant.

summary: Responsive Images and Media is easiest to learn by connecting syntax to a rendered result.
Keep selectors readable and test the effect in the browser.
Verify compatibility and accessibility when the feature or interface requires it.
